deals.title: Ops Cloud — Network Visibility
deals.welcome: Dana, thanks for the time last week. This room keeps everything from our conversations in one place: the discovery recap, the two-site evaluation we sketched out, and the materials your team asked for. Add anyone who should be in the loop.

execSummary.problem:
Halvorsen runs 14 cross-dock and warehouse sites on three different WMS instances, and exception handling (late trailers, short picks, dock congestion) still lives in email threads and a shared spreadsheet refreshed twice a day. Site leaders learn about a missed carrier cutoff after it has already turned into a chargeback.

Leadership wants one operational picture of the network before peak season, and the current reporting stack can't deliver it without a multi-quarter data project that IT has no capacity for until the ERP upgrade finishes.
challenges: No real-time view across three WMS instances; the network report is assembled by hand every morning
Carrier chargebacks for missed cutoffs reached $410K last year and are trending up
Exception handling depends on a few experienced site leads, which makes peak staffing fragile
IT is committed to the ERP upgrade through Q2 and can't take on a custom integration build
solutions: Pre-built connectors for all three WMS instances, live in weeks with no custom build for IT
Exception rules that flag at-risk carrier cutoffs 90 minutes out and route them to the right site lead
One live network dashboard that replaces the manual morning report
Resolution playbooks that capture how the best site leads handle exceptions, so newer leads follow the same steps

discovery.summary: Halvorsen is a mid-market 3PL (about $620M revenue, 14 sites) heading into peak season with fragmented visibility across three WMS instances. The pain is concentrated in missed carrier cutoffs and a manual morning report. Dana Whitfield (VP Operations) is sponsoring a two-site evaluation and wants a decision before the December budget lock.
corporateStrategy: Grow e-commerce fulfillment revenue 25% by consolidating smaller shippers onto shared sites
Standardize operations across the two sites acquired in the last 18 months
Protect margin during peak by cutting chargebacks and overtime
topOutcomes: Reduce carrier chargebacks at least 30% in the first peak season
Replace the manual morning network report with a live dashboard
Resolve dock exceptions in under 30 minutes instead of hours
challenges: Three WMS instances with no common data layer
Missed carrier cutoffs discovered after the fact
Morning network report takes an analyst about 2 hours a day
Tribal knowledge concentrated in a handful of senior site leads
jobsToBeDone: See every at-risk outbound shipment across all sites before the carrier cutoff
Route an exception to the right site lead with context, not a forwarded email
Show leadership network performance without assembling it by hand
discovery.primaryUseCase: Network-wide exception management: detect at-risk outbound shipments across all 14 sites and route them to site leads with a recommended action before the carrier cutoff.

90 Days: Two-site evaluation live in Columbus and Memphis
Baseline chargeback and exception-resolution metrics captured
1 Year: All 14 sites on one network dashboard
Beyond: Extend exception rules to inbound and yard management
Use network performance data to price new shipper contracts

meddpic.economicBuyer:
Not confirmed yet. Dana believes the CFO, Greg Ellison, signs anything over $75K.
Ask Dana for an introduction once the evaluation plan is agreed, framed around the chargeback numbers.
meddpic.decisionCriteria:
Early read from Dana:
1. Connects to all three WMS instances without an IT project
2. Live at two sites inside 60 days
3. Per-site pricing that works for the smaller acquired sites

tasks.task: Discovery call with Dana and site leadership
Share discovery recap and proposed evaluation scope
Pull last 90 days of chargeback data for the baseline
tasks.notes: Leon is exporting carrier invoices from the TMS. Dana asked that we use Columbus and Memphis as the baseline sites.

tasks.task: Technical fit call: WMS connectors and data access
Day-in-the-life demo using Columbus exception data
Build chargeback-reduction business case with Finance
Confirm procurement path and vendor onboarding requirements

deals.title: Ops Cloud — Patient Flow Pilot
deals.welcome: Samantha and team, this is our shared workspace for the Brightwater patient-flow pilot. The success criteria we agreed on, the security review packet, and the weekly pilot readouts all live here, and the action plan shows who owns what through the go/no-go decision.

execSummary.problem:
Brightwater's three hospitals run near capacity, and discharge delays are the main constraint. Patients cleared for discharge wait an average of 5.2 hours for transport, pharmacy, or paperwork. Bed management is coordinated by phone and a whiteboard in each house supervisor's office, so nobody can see where the next available bed is coming from.

ED boarding hours are up 18% year over year and are now a board-level quality metric. The CFO has set aside capacity funds, contingent on proving a solution in a live pilot.
challenges: Discharge-to-departure time averages 5.2 hours, holding beds the ED needs
Bed status lives on whiteboards and phone calls with no system-wide view
ED boarding hours up 18% year over year, now tracked by the board quality committee
Any system touching patient data must clear InfoSec review with HIPAA and HITRUST requirements
solutions: Live capacity view across all three hospitals, fed from the Epic ADT stream
Discharge milestone tracking that flags stalled discharges before noon
Automated handoffs to transport and pharmacy the moment a discharge order is signed
Security package: SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST r2 in progress, signed BAA, and U.S.-only data residency

discovery.summary: Brightwater (3 hospitals, 1,100 beds) is piloting Ops Cloud on two medical-surgical units at St. Anne's to prove it can cut discharge delays. Samantha Cole (VP Patient Flow) is our champion, the CFO has earmarked capacity funds contingent on pilot results, and InfoSec review is the gating item before production data.
corporateStrategy: Grow surgical volume 12% without adding licensed beds
Reduce ED boarding as part of the 2027 quality plan
Consolidate operational tools onto fewer, better-integrated platforms
topOutcomes: Cut discharge-to-departure time from 5.2 to under 3.5 hours on pilot units
Raise discharges before noon from 14% to 30%
Reduce ED boarding hours 20% within the first year
challenges: No shared, real-time bed status across the three hospitals
Discharge tasks (transport, pharmacy, education) coordinated by phone
Nurse managers spend about 6 hours a week chasing discharge status
InfoSec requires HITRUST alignment and a full risk assessment for any EHR-connected tool
jobsToBeDone: Know which beds will open in the next four hours
Clear the path for a discharge the moment the order is signed
Report capacity metrics to the board without manual chart pulls
discovery.primaryUseCase: Discharge acceleration and capacity visibility for med-surg units, starting with 4 West and 5 East at St. Anne's and expanding to all three hospitals.

90 Days: Pilot live on 4 West and 5 East with a read-only ADT feed
Go/no-go decision against the agreed success criteria
1 Year: All med-surg units across three hospitals live
Beyond: Tie capacity forecasts into nurse staffing plans

meddpic.decisionCriteria:
1. Pilot hits at least 2 of 3 success criteria (discharge time, before-noon rate, nurse manager hours)
2. Clears the InfoSec risk assessment with no high findings
3. Uses the existing Epic ADT interface, no new interface build
4. Year-one cost inside the $250K capacity fund
meddpic.decisionProcess:
Pilot readout to the Capacity Steering Committee (chaired by Samantha)
→ InfoSec sign-off from Kevin Walsh
→ CFO approval (Robert Chen)
→ Contract through Supply Chain
The steering committee meets the first Tuesday of each month; target decision is the next meeting after the final readout.

tasks.task: Capacity discovery workshop with the patient flow team
Agree pilot success criteria and baseline metrics
Executive alignment call with the COO
Tailored demo using de-identified St. Anne's census data
Pilot kickoff on 4 West and 5 East
Connect read-only ADT feed in the test environment
InfoSec risk assessment and HITRUST questionnaire
tasks.notes: Kevin flagged data retention and SSO (Azure AD) requirements. Ridgeline Security is sending written responses and the pen-test summary by Friday.

tasks.task: Final pilot readout to the Capacity Steering Committee
Review capacity ROI model with Finance
BAA and MSA review with Legal

deals.title: Ops Cloud — Plant Floor Visibility
deals.welcome: Michelle, Tom, and team, here's everything for the Castellan decision in one place: the proposal and pricing options, the business case we built with Finance, and the path to signature. We'll keep the action plan current after every conversation.

execSummary.problem:
Castellan's four plants run on a mix of MES data, paper travelers, and a nightly Excel roll-up, so the operations team sees yesterday's scrap and downtime, not today's. Unplanned downtime cost an estimated $2.1M last year, and on-time delivery slipped to 88% against a 95% commitment to tier-one OEM customers.

Two of Castellan's largest OEM customers have asked for a corrective action plan ahead of their Q1 supplier reviews, and a previous in-house MES analytics project stalled after 14 months.
challenges: Downtime and scrap are reported a day late, after the shift that caused them
On-time delivery at 88% against a 95% commitment to key OEM customers
Plant managers spend Monday mornings reconciling spreadsheets instead of running the floor
A previous MES analytics project stalled after 14 months and $600K
solutions: Connect MES and ERP data from all four plants into one live operations view
Shift-level alerts on scrap and downtime thresholds, routed to the line supervisor
Standard OTD and OEE dashboards that replace the nightly Excel roll-up
Phased rollout with two plants live in 8 weeks on a fixed-fee implementation

discovery.summary: Castellan (4 plants, $480M revenue) needs shift-level visibility to fix on-time delivery before OEM customer reviews in Q1. Michelle Park (VP Operations) is championing; Tom Brennan (COO) owns the budget. The business case is built and the proposal is with Finance. The open questions are phasing and year-one price.
corporateStrategy: Restore 95% on-time delivery for tier-one OEM customers
Lift OEE from 61% to 70% across all plants by 2027
Make plant operations data-driven ahead of a planned fifth-plant acquisition
topOutcomes: On-time delivery back to 95% within two quarters
Eliminate the nightly Excel roll-up (about 30 analyst hours a week)
challenges: Next-day reporting on scrap and downtime
OTD at 88% with two OEM corrective-action requests open
Weekly manual reconciliation across four plants
Low trust in analytics projects after the stalled MES initiative
jobsToBeDone: Catch a scrap spike during the shift, not the next morning
Give the COO one view of all four plants
Prove to OEM customers that corrective actions are working
discovery.primaryUseCase: Shift-level production monitoring: live OEE, scrap, and downtime across four plants, with alerts routed to line supervisors.

90 Days: OEM corrective action plan backed by live OTD data
1 Year: All four plants live with OEE at 66%+
Beyond: Onboard the fifth plant within 60 days of acquisition

meddpic.decisionCriteria:
1. Live at two plants in 8 weeks on a fixed-fee implementation
2. Native connectors for Rockwell MES and Epicor ERP, no custom build
3. Year-one cost under $160K
4. References from two discrete manufacturers
meddpic.decisionProcess:
Michelle recommends
→ Tom Brennan (COO) approves budget
→ Linda Marsh (CFO) signs anything over $100K
→ Legal reviews the MSA on Castellan paper
→ Procurement issues the PO
Tom wants a decision before the Q4 operations review.

tasks.task: Plant tour and line-supervisor interviews in Dayton
Technical deep dive: Rockwell MES and Epicor connectors
Build downtime and OTD business case with Finance
Pricing review with Tom and Linda
tasks.notes: Tom prefers Option B (two plants in year one, the other two in year two). Linda wants the implementation fee spread across the first two invoices.

tasks.task: Reference calls with two discrete manufacturers

deals.title: Ops Cloud — Member Service Operations
deals.welcome: Brian, this room holds the final proposal, the redlined agreement, and the remaining steps to get Meridian live before the new-year member service push.

execSummary.problem:
Meridian's member service center handles about 42,000 contacts a month across phone, chat, and branches, but loan and account-maintenance requests are tracked in three disconnected queues. A routine request takes 3.5 business days on average, and member satisfaction scores for service fell six points last year.

Leadership has committed to a 24-hour turnaround standard for 2027, and the last NCUA exam asked for stronger audit trails on account changes.
challenges: Requests split across three queues with no single view of the backlog
3.5-day average turnaround against a 24-hour goal
Member satisfaction for service down six points year over year
NCUA exam findings call for better audit trails on account changes
solutions: One operations queue across phone, chat, and branch requests
SLA timers and escalation rules built around the 24-hour standard
Audit-ready history on every account-maintenance request
Pre-built connector for Meridian's Symitar core

discovery.summary: Meridian ($2.3B in assets, 21 branches) selected Ops Cloud to unify member service queues. Commercial terms are close, but the CFO hasn't engaged directly and the room has been quiet for over a week while Legal works through the redlines.
corporateStrategy: Deliver a 24-hour service standard for routine member requests
Grow membership 8% through digital-first service
Strengthen compliance posture ahead of the next NCUA exam
topOutcomes: Recover the six-point drop in service satisfaction
Complete audit trail on 100% of account changes
challenges: Three disconnected request queues
No SLA tracking or escalation
Manual audit evidence gathering before exams
Branch staff re-key requests into the core
jobsToBeDone: See every open member request in one place
Escalate before a request breaches SLA
Hand examiners a complete audit trail
discovery.primaryUseCase: Member service operations: one queue and SLA tracking for loan and account-maintenance requests across the contact center and 21 branches.

90 Days: Contact center live on the unified queue
SLA reporting in place for leadership
Beyond: Member-facing request status in online banking

meddpic.decisionCriteria:
1. Symitar integration without a core-vendor change order
2. 24-hour SLA reporting out of the box
3. NCUA-ready audit trail
4. Three-year cost inside the $300K budget line
meddpic.decisionProcess:
Brian (SVP Member Experience) selected Ridgeline
→ Legal redlines the MSA
→ Diane Foster (CFO) approves contracts over $75K
→ ALCO committee notified (no vote needed)
→ Signature
Diane hasn't joined a meeting yet. Brian says she "trusts his call", which needs testing before the close date.

tasks.task: Contact center demo with team leads
CFO business case review with Diane Foster
tasks.notes: Rescheduled twice. Ask Brian to set the meeting directly with Diane and keep it to 20 minutes on the three-year cost and the audit-trail requirement.

deals.title: Ops Cloud — Store Operations Rollout
deals.welcome: Welcome to the Oakline onboarding room. Now that we're signed, this space tracks the rollout: kickoff notes, the requirements we've captured, the implementation plan, and the training schedule for all 180 stores.

execSummary.problem:
Oakline's 180 stores run replenishment, labor scheduling, and store tasks through separate tools, and district managers spend Monday mornings compiling store performance by hand. Out-of-stocks on top-selling SKUs averaged 7.8%, and store task completion was invisible between district visits.

A four-week pilot in 12 stores cut out-of-stocks from 7.8% to 5.1%, and Oakline signed a three-year agreement to roll out chain-wide in three regional waves.
challenges: Out-of-stocks on top-selling SKUs averaging 7.8%
District managers compile weekly store performance by hand
No visibility into store task completion between visits
Seasonal labor planning disconnected from traffic and replenishment data
solutions: Store operations dashboard for all 180 stores and 14 districts
Out-of-stock alerts tied to replenishment exceptions
Store task tracking with completion visibility for district managers
Phased regional rollout with a train-the-trainer program

discovery.summary: Oakline signed a three-year agreement after a four-week pilot in 12 stores cut out-of-stocks from 7.8% to 5.1%. The rollout covers all 180 stores in three regional waves, starting with the Southeast (62 stores).
corporateStrategy: Grow comparable store sales 4% through better in-stock performance
Standardize store operations after the Evergreen Market acquisition
Shift district managers from reporting to coaching
topOutcomes: Give each district manager back 6 hours a week
challenges: Replenishment exceptions surfaced too late to act on
Manual weekly store performance reporting
Inconsistent store execution across districts
Two store systems after the Evergreen acquisition
jobsToBeDone: Fix an out-of-stock before the customer notices
Know which stores completed this week's tasks
Coach store managers with facts, not anecdotes
discovery.primaryUseCase: Store operations management: in-stock alerts, store task tracking, and district performance reporting across 180 stores.

Beyond: Extend to the Evergreen Market banner

meddpic.decisionCriteria:
1. Pilot proves a 2+ point out-of-stock reduction
2. Integrates with Manhattan WMS and Oracle Retail
3. All 180 stores rolled out within two quarters
4. Three-year cost under $850K
meddpic.decisionProcess:
Pilot readout
→ Executive steering review (Rachel Summers, COO)
→ CFO approval (Dennis Ward)
→ MSA and order form
→ Signed

tasks.task: Store operations demo with district managers
Integration review: Manhattan WMS and Oracle Retail

experience.task: Executive kickoff with Rachel and Jason
Introduce the implementation team and weekly cadence
Confirm success metrics and rollout waves

experience.notes: Store hierarchy loaded. 58 of 62 stores validated; 4 Evergreen-converted stores need a location-code mapping from Aisha's team.
